title: Micro-Prescription Hint Rail — wireframe + backlog
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight wireframe and backlog for an inline "micro-prescription" hint rail that surfaces Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, quantization) directly in the model route and eval views. The goal is to reduce discovery friction and make unit-economics gains more actionable for engineers without forcing a full onboarding flow into Optimize.

Design hypothesis:
- Engineers prefer concise, contextual suggestions tied to observed traffic patterns rather than a separate modal or long checklist.
- Presenting a short actionable step + expected cost/delta + confidence score will increase take rate and lower per-token spend.
- Allowing one-click quick-apply for safe heuristics (non-destructive) will be critical for velocity.

Key UX components (wireframe notes):
1) Hint Rail (right-side, collapsible)
   - Compact header: "Optimize suggestions (3)" with chevron collapse state.
   - Each row = recommendation card: short title, severity (info/advise/high-impact), economic delta (est. tokens / month saved), confidence (low/medium/high), and one-line rationale.
   - Interactive affordances: Preview (simulate impact), Quick Apply (apply preset), Details (open inspector panel), and Undo (available for 5m after apply).
   - Keyboard accessible: tab-focusable rows, Enter opens Details, Space triggers Quick Apply confirmation modal.

2) Recommendation Card anatomy
   - Title: e.g., "Batch by 8 for chat endpoints"
   - Delta pill: "~$420/month" (derived from traffic buckets)
   - Confidence ribbon (color-coded) with tooltip explaining telemetry used (p95 latency, queue depth, tail-kv cache hits)
   - Short rationale line: "High throughput, short messages — batching yields 2.6x peak token throughput."
   - Small CTA group: [Preview][Quick Apply] · link "why this?" leads to inspector.

3) Inspector panel (slide-over)
   - Top: recom summary + time series sparkline for latency and cost change if applied.
   - Middle: detailed simulation parameters (sample input distribution, sequence length percentiles, hardware profile assumptions).
   - Bottom: Rollout controls: apply to 10% canary, apply to route, schedule, or pin to model version.
   - Safety note and rollback path.

4) Sim Preview modal (lightweight)
   - Show before/after latency and cost per 1M tokens, example output diffs (detect hallucination risk via eval hooks) and a small sample of prompts the sim used.
   - Toggle quantization aggressive vs safe profile to show quality delta.

Backlog (prioritized):
- P0: Hint rail container + collapsed state + static sample cards (skeleton data) for dev testing (Frontend) — 2 sprints.
- P0: Quick Apply (non-destructive) that stashes preset and triggers an API call to create a temporary config in staging; includes toast and 5m undo — 1 sprint backend + 1 sprint frontend.
- P1: Simulation engine endpoint that consumes route histogram and returns delta estimates (cost, latency, quality proxies) — 2 sprints infra/algorithms.
- P1: Inspector slide-over with traffic sampling preview and rollout control (canary) + audit log linkage — 2 sprints.
- P2: Confidence scoring model (meta-heuristic) that uses historical rollout outcomes and telemetry to tune confidence levels — research spike 1 sprint + implementation 2 sprints.
- P2: Accessibility pass: screen reader labels, high-contrast, keyboard flows — 1 sprint.
- P3: Integrations: feature flagging for Dedicated/private customers, RBAC gating, and console permissions — 1 sprint.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to persist applied quick-presets? (route-level config vs ephemeral user-level override) — preference toward route-level with explicit revert.
- How to compute accurate economic deltas for mixed-model routes that use tool-calls or function-calling? Need a heuristics fallback.
- Quantization preview: do we show binary "safe/aggressive" presets or a slider? Slider more expressive but more educational burden.
- Rollouts: default to 10% canary with automatic rollback if latency increases > 10% or error rate increases > 1% — need SRE buy-in.

Acceptance criteria (for initial launch):
- Rail appears on model route page when recommendations exist; shows correct counts and accessible collapsed state.
- Quick Apply triggers creation of a staged config and surface toast with undo.
- Inspector shows simulation results and a traffic sparkline that matches last 24h telemetry within reasonable bounds.
- Telemetry events emitted for impressions, previews, quick-applies, accepts, and rollbacks.
- E2E test coverage for keyboard flows and undo semantics.

Metrics to track (KR-focused):
- Take rate: % of users who apply at least one suggestion per active route.
- Cost delta: aggregate estimated $/month saved for applied suggestions (compare baseline month over month).
- False positive rate: % of applied suggestions that had rollback within 7 days.
- Time-to-apply: median time from impression to quick-apply click.

Rollout plan:
- Internal dogfood: 2 weeks on core product routes (console + infra teams) — collect qualitative feedback.
- Beta: opt-in for accounts with >$5k/month inference spend for 4 weeks. Closely monitor KR metrics and SLOs.
- GA: gradual ramp to 100% of accounts with recommendation source enabled, add RBAC gating for enterprise tenants.

Dev notes / quick sketches to hand to frontend:
- Use existing suggestion-card component but add delta pill and confidence chip.
- Rail width 340px, collapsible to 56px minimized icon.
- Use design tokens: warning/orange for medium-impact, red for high-impact; green for high-confidence.
- Localize cost formatting based on account currency.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: noisy/incorrect recommendations erode trust. Mitigation: conservative defaults, require 10% canary, easy rollback, and clear confidence indicators.
- Risk: simulated savings not matching reality for long-tail inputs. Mitigation: show sample prompts used in sim and provide a link to run longer evals in Optimize.

Next steps (this week):
- UX: small | hi-fidelity mockups for collapsed vs expanded states (Maya) — due Thu.
- Eng: proto Quick Apply API spec (Liam) — due Fri.
- Research: prepare a 1-page note on confidence heuristics and telemetry signals (Diego) — due Mon.

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas (informal):
- Consider "nudge" email for routes that have >15% waste and no Optimize interactions in 30 days.
- Explore embedding a tiny simulation runner in the client for rough immediate estimates (cheap) and server calculate exact.
- Maybe surface a "why not applied" signal if a user dismisses recommendations — quick survey modal?

---
End of draft.
